_what: What each place a message is written to can show, as one capability record per surface (src/surface-compose.mjs). `html` whether markup inside the text is shown; `collapsibles` whether a folded section is supported; `checkboxes` whether a task-list item is drawn as a box; `dialect` the text format, a row of `dialects`; `max_chars` the longest body, or null for no limit; `theme`: how a picture that has a light and a dark form is written ('picture' two sources in one element, 'suffix' two images told apart by an address suffix, 'single' only the light one). `unproven` names the capabilities of that row nobody has confirmed against the real surface: a composition that relies on one reports it, so it is checked before it is trusted. Composition reads these fields and never the surface's name. A new surface is a new row. `dialects`: how each text format writes each block, filled from the block (`{hashes}` a heading's or a folded section's marks, `{text}`, `{alt}`, `{url}`, `{mark}`): `plain_text` strips markup characters and keeps a link's words; `heading`, `code`, `list_item`, `folded`; `boxes` the item and its two marks when the place draws boxes (null: none in this format); `image`, and `themed_images` whether the light and dark forms (`theme`) can be written in it; `html_blocks` whether a folded section may be written as markup; `counts_as_used` whether writing in it relies on the place's `dialect` capability (so an unconfirmed one is reported). A new text format is a new row.
